The claim reports this as a mixing risk (effects mostly unwanted; pleasant and liking ratings not different) and gives the amounts only once, as labelled study conditions in the precise statement. The later mean peak (2.9 against 2.1 hours, not tested) stays in the statement as a finding, not in the plain lines. cl_benzo_harm_reduction_services: the authors read drug checking as having consistent positive outcomes; the editors' reading is insufficient evidence, because no design could show an effect on harm. Both are now shown; confirm.

One decision for two answers (cl_benzo_harm_reduction_services, reader 283; cl_benzo_own_practices, reader 282): Gelberg et al.'s fold sizes (a positive test-strip result went with a four-fold reduction in quantity used overall; 20-fold when benzodiazepines were tested, tenfold for stimulants, twofold for opioids) are reported in the review's Table 1 without a description of the measure. After 283_patch_2.json, both answers give the study as reported behaviour, most strongly when benzodiazepines were tested, and keep the sizes in their anchors only, with the same numbers. If the sizes are to be shown, show them in both magnitudes with the same wording; my reading is to keep them in the anchors until the primary paper has been read.

Cross-group (reader 282): Park et al. figures agree in both answers (68 of 103; 96% to 68%; 69%), and so do the Gelberg figures (541 adults; 28 days; four-fold; 20-fold). The phrase '45, interviewed' in cl_benzo_own_practices is replaced in 282's patch by 'in a qualitative study', which matches the review and the card.

cl_opi_using_alone, pages: the survey covered people using any illicit drug (past-week crystal meth 72.9%, opioids 70.0%), and crack or cocaine use was one of the two correlates; the answer may also belong on the methamphetamine and cocaine pages. The plain line keeps the coroners' 69% as cited background with no definitions; confirm.
